These rewards force the model to learn actions as consistent state operators rather than memorized temporal patterns, and extend naturally to out-of-distribution composite action cycles that the base model handles poorly. We further release CycleBench, a diagnostic benchmark for state-returning ability under complex action structures. WorldCycle reduces state returning drift by up to 44% and lifts composite-action accuracy nearly 4x over the base model, providing a vital foundation for physically grounded world models.

papers.title: GAUGE: A Measurement-Grounded Benchmark for Physical Fidelity in Simulation Engines and Video World Models
papers.authors: Shuai Wang, Yaxin Feng, Xuekun Jiang, Shihan Tian, Ningyu Yan, Xing Shen, Chaoyang Lyu, Hui Wang, Yunsong Zhou, Hanqing Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Yang Xiang, Xing Gao, Chunhua Shen, Weinan Zhang
papers.abstract: Physics engines facilitate large-scale training and evaluation for embodied intelligence, while generative video world models are emerging as implicit simulators of future states and interactions. However, existing evaluations of physical fidelity are often conducted in isolation and rely heavily on perceptual similarity or human judgments, providing limited insight into which physical principles or parameters are violated. We introduce GAUGE, a real-world-grounded diagnostic benchmark for jointly evaluating how numerical simulators and generative video world models reproduce or deviate from real-world physics. It comprises 22 controlled task families covering rigid bodies, flexible cables, textiles, and volumetric deformable objects. Grounded in real-world trajectories and paired with calibrated physical metadata, uncertainty annotations, and task-specific observables, these tasks cover fundamental physical processes including collision, friction, momentum transfer, oscillation, self-contact, and deformation across diverse materials and conditions. We benchmark Isaac Sim, Genesis, and Newton on 14 task families using generalized trajectory errors, and evaluate 6 image-to-video models on 5 rigid-body tasks by testing physical-law consistency and the temporal stability of inferred parameters. Our results reveal no uniformly faithful physics engine, with the largest discrepancies arising in impulsive contact, rapid textile motion, and volumetric deformation. We further find that video world models can produce trajectories with the expected equation form while recovering incorrect accelerations, momentum transfer, and oscillation timing. GAUGE lays the groundwork for developing more physically faithful simulators and world models for embodied intelligence.

papers.title: PhyLatent: Learning Dynamics-Relevant Representations for JEPA World Models
papers.authors: Xi Zeng, Haojie Ren, Ziying Song
papers.abstract: We propose PhyLatent, a dynamics-relevant training objective for JointEmbedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models. Our key observation is that preventing global latent collapse does not ensure that a representation preserves physical states and action consequences. We identify three failure modes in JEPA world models: physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, and counterfactual dynamics collapse. PhyLatent addresses them through three training pathways: physical invariance, physical identifiability, and counterfactual dynamics, implemented with physical state grounding, future representation alignment, static visual invariance, counterfactual branch separation, and latent denoising. On OGBench-Cube, PhyLatent reduces the three failure rates from 15.60%, 6.71%, and 8.41% to 7.53%, 0.95%, and 4.62%, respectively, and improves model predictive control (MPC) success from 70.0% to 78.1%. With the same architecture and planner, it further improves success from 81.0% to 98.0% on TwoRooms and remains competitive on Reacher and PushT. These results show that global non-collapse alone is insufficient for learning a reliable JEPA worldmodel state space.

papers.title: HERA: Historical Evidence Routing Adapter for Physical Prediction in Latent World Models
papers.authors: Yuanruyi, Yue Cao, Haojia Gao, Guanqiu Guo,  Ziyuezhang,  Shangqin, Junbo Tan, Bokui Chen, Zhuo Zou, Xueqian Wang
papers.abstract: Predictive video models have emerged as promising world models by learning latent visual dynamics from large-scale video. Yet these models remain challenged by physical events under occlusion, where later predictions may depend on object evidence that is no longer available in the current view. Addressing this challenge requires historical evidence not only to be preserved but also to remain accessible when it becomes relevant to a subsequent prediction. Existing approaches mainly enlarge the temporal context, cache generic video features, or impose explicit object-centric states, thereby improving the capacity or structure of retained history. However, they do not directly address how relevant historical evidence can be selectively retrieved and integrated into a pretrained predictor without interfering with its native latent workspace. Accordingly, we introduce HERA (Historical Evidence Routing Adapter), a framework for routing retained historical evidence into a frozen latent predictor, and instantiate it with Register-Routed Patch Memory (RRPM), a lightweight adapter comprising a Structured Memory Bank, Memory Registers, and Workspace Registers. On the IntPhys2 Main split, HERA with RRPM improves the pairwise AvgSurprise accuracy of V-JEPA 2-G from 52.57% to 54.35%. Subgroup analysis shows particularly strong improvements on fixed-camera continuity, from 46.15% to 57.69%, and fixed-camera immutability, from 46.15% to 63.46%. These results support historical evidence routing as a practical adaptation strategy for physical prediction in latent world models.

papers.title: Failure Detection for Surgical Robot Imitation Policies via Flow-Matching World Modeling
papers.authors: Zhefeng Huang, Yilin Cai, Ankit Patel, Mohammad Hajiha, Brendan Browne, Yue Chen
papers.abstract: Introduces FoMo-FD (Flow-Matching World Model for Failure Detection): uses flow-matching world model to detect failures in imitation-learning surgical robot policies, addressing scarce failure data, variable manipulation dynamics, and balancing missed detections vs. disruptive false alarms for safe deployment in safety-critical surgical tasks.

papers.title: Cross-Embodiment Transfer via Behavior-Aligned Representations
papers.authors: Ajay Sridhar, Jensen Gao, Jonathan Yang, Jean Mercat, Suneel Belkhale, Dorsa Sadigh
papers.abstract: Studies role of behavior-aligned representations (object bounding boxes, language motions, end-effector traces of robot motion) in vision-language-action (VLA) models to promote cross-embodiment transfer. Hypothesizes representations invariant across embodiments while predictive of robot actions improve transfer. Examines how these representations enable VLA models to bridge embodiment gaps in large-scale imitation learning.

papers.title: X-NavDP: Generalizing Navigation Diffusion Policy to Novel Behavior and Embodiments with Group Q-score Reweighted Matching
papers.authors: Tianyu Yang, Yiming Zeng, Wenzhe Cai, Yuqiang Yang, Jiaqi Peng, Hui Cheng, Jiangmiao Pang, Tai Wang
papers.abstract: Pretraining navigation diffusion policies relies on large-scale expert demonstrations from a fully-informed oracle planner suited to a single nominal robot, limiting generalization to diverse embodiments and challenging scenarios (dead ends, long detours) needing diverse local reactive behaviors with onboard local observations. Proposes RL post-training with Group Q-score Reweighted Matching to improve navigation diffusion policy generalization to novel behaviors and embodiments.

papers.title: ShadowDancer: Teaching Video World Models Any Action by Learning Unified Dynamics
papers.authors: Jin Cao, Zian Meng, Kaipeng Zhang
papers.abstract: ShadowDancer enables any-action, frame-level control of interactive video world models via 'shadow pairs' (video pairs replaying same dynamics under resampled appearance) and cross-shadow prediction. Learns a unified dynamics representation in a block-causal world model; any demonstrated clip becomes a reusable action asset replayed in new scenes without action labels, motion estimators, or fine-tuning. 86% average blinded win rate in rollout comparisons vs latent-action and interactive WM baselines.

papers.title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language
papers.authors: Shuyao Shang, Yuqi Wang, Ruopeng Gao, Xu Chen, Tieniu Tan, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang
papers.abstract: PhiZero introduces 'physical language', a compact discrete representation of world-state transitions, learned self-supervised from in-the-wild videos. Adopts reason-then-render paradigm: infers future evolution as physical-language sequence, then renders to video. Enables physically coherent world evolution, realistic interactive modeling, fine-grained action-conditioned simulation, and zero-shot motion transfer.

papers.title: RedFlow: Redirect Failure into Action-Level Corrections for Flow-matching VLA Policies
papers.authors: Zhengyang Yan, Junhao Li, Fangqi Zhu, Zijun Wang, Quanxin Shou, Yikun Miao, Xiaoyi Pang, Zicong Hong, Song Guo
papers.abstract: RedFlow is a fine-grained offline RL framework that redirects failure experiences into action-level corrective supervision for flow-matching VLA policies. Combines Context-Aware Corrective Matching (identifies failure-inducing actions, retrieves successful alternatives as corrective targets) with an Adaptive Redirection Objective. Improves real-world success rate from 56.7% to 74.7% on LIBERO + 3 real manipulation tasks, matching on-policy PPO/GRPO/DDPO with ~10x fewer samples.

papers.title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization
papers.authors: Zhoushun Yu, Xiaoyu Hu, Xiangyu Xu
papers.abstract: QQWorld replaces LeWorldModel's Epps-Pulley (EP) latent regularization with quantile-quantile matching that aligns projected latent samples with rank-matched Gaussian quantiles, maintaining corrective gradients in heavy tails. Adds cross-batch QQ enlarging the ranking pool via detached previous-batch samples. Improves planning success rate of LeWM across four control environments with better Gaussian alignment and thinner latent tails.

papers.title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
papers.authors: Dongxiu Liu, Haoyi Niu, Peng Cheng, Yuan Gao, Xirui Kang, Sangli Teng, Koushil Sreenath, Xianyuan Zhan
papers.abstract: ODEWorld learns a continuous latent velocity field (PT-Flow) operating in physical time, with dynamics parameterized by an ODE in latent space. Prediction becomes temporal integration via an ODE solver. Addresses representation collapse in latent WMs, supports arbitrary temporal resolution and backward prediction, and provides planning-oriented information for policy learning. Excels in both video generation and robotic control.

papers.title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.authors: Xiangcheng Zhang, Yilun Du
papers.abstract: World Action Planner leverages action-conditioned world models for generalizable decision-making. Uses world model rollouts to evaluate and select actions across tasks without task-specific training, targeting zero-shot generalization of world-model-based planning across embodiments and environments.

papers.title: FA-RDP: A Frequency-Adaptive Reactive Diffusion Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.authors: Lifeng Zhuo, Wendi Chen, Han Xue, Shirun Tang, Jun Lv
papers.abstract: FA-RDP is a frequency-adaptive reactive diffusion policy for contact-rich manipulation, adapting policy frequency to contact dynamics to maintain stability under reactive/high-bandwidth manipulation settings.

papers.title: Towards Real-Time PixOOD: Efficient Anomaly Segmentation for Autonomous Vehicles
papers.authors: Luca de Martino, Federico Aromolo, Federico Nesti, Giorgio Buttazzo
papers.abstract: Real-time efficient anomaly/out-of-distribution segmentation for autonomous vehicle perception, targeting deployment-time inference cost reduction while maintaining PixOOD-level detection quality.

papers.title: AuricularWorld: Hierarchical Action-Guided World Modeling for Fine-Grained Auricular Reasoning
papers.authors: Jingwen Yang, Senmao Wang, Luoyao Kang, Runmeng Cui, Keying Zhang
papers.abstract: AuricularWorld applies hierarchical action-guided world modeling to fine-grained auricular (ear/medicine) reasoning, extending action-conditioned world model ideas to specialized domain reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Security of World-Model-Based Embodied AI: A Lifecycle of Threats, Defenses, and Open Challenges
papers.authors: Fazhong Liu, Zhuoyan Chen, Haozhen Tan, Yan Meng, Guoxing Chen
papers.abstract: Survey on security of world-model-based embodied AI across the lifecycle: threat models (perception, planning, control attacks), defense mechanisms, and open challenges. Relevant to robustness of world models in autonomous driving and robotics.

papers.title: FinSMART: Financial Sentiment Analysis for Algorithmic Trading through Market-Aligned Learning
papers.authors: Giorgos Iacovides, Wuyang Zhou, Danilo Mandic
papers.abstract: FinSMART performs financial sentiment analysis for algorithmic trading via market-aligned learning, aligning model supervision with market-movement signals rather than raw labels to improve trading-relevant sentiment prediction.

papers.title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
papers.authors: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang, Di Xu, Yingying Zhu, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai, Han Ding
papers.abstract: TurboVLA reformulates the conventional V->L->A pathway as a direct V+L->A mapping, independently encoding visual observations and language instructions with lightweight bidirectional vision-language interaction and compact action decoder. Achieves 97.7% success on LIBERO with 0.2B params, 31.2ms latency, 0.9GB VRAM on RTX 4090.

papers.title: Mitigating Compounding Error via Video Representation Regularization
papers.authors: Taiye Chen, Qi Zhang, Yisen Wang
papers.abstract: Investigates internal representation dynamics of video diffusion world models, discovers compounding error is coupled with dimensional collapse of hidden representations. Proposes video representation regularization to stabilize latent representations. Improves Aesthetic Quality from 38.65 to 55.56 on VBench.

papers.title: HeteroPROMPT: A Real-time and Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception Framework
papers.authors: Armin Maleki, Hayder Radha
papers.abstract: Privacy-preserving collaborative perception framework aligning heterogeneous agents' BEV features via modular prompts. Lightweight tuning with frozen encoders/fusion. Improves AP over SOTA on OPV2V-H and V2XSet with orders-of-magnitude fewer trainable params.

papers.title: DVPSFormer: Efficient Online Depth-aware Video Panoptic Segmentation for Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Yung-Hsu Yang, Luigi Piccinelli, Siyuan Li, Mattia Segu, Lei Ke
papers.abstract: Unified online architecture for depth-aware video panoptic segmentation. Explicit scene discretization (ESD) with discrete-to-continuous depth head. SOTA on Cityscapes-DVPS and SemKITTI-DVPS benchmarks.

papers.title: Controlled Experiments on Lane Changing by Transitional Autonomous Vehicle: Dataset and Behavioral Insights
papers.authors: Abhinav Sharma, Md Abdullah Al Hasan, Danjue Chen, George F. List
papers.abstract: NC-tALC dataset: controlled field experiments on mandatory lane-changing behavior of transitional AVs. 78 lane-change trials on public road, RTK-GNSS/INS trajectories, lead-lag gap analysis, surrogate safety measures.

papers.title: Object Detection for Autonomous Driving in Chinese Rural Scenes: An Experimental Study on Real-Synthetic Data Mixing
papers.authors: Danning Zhu, Ziyan Lin, Jing Wu
papers.abstract: Real-synthetic mixed object detection dataset for Chinese rural roads. Evaluates 13 detectors (YOLO series, RT-DETR) with 14-category system including electric tricycles, low-speed vehicles. YOLO11m achieves mAP@0.5 of 0.758.

papers.title: NeoRacer: An Open, Standardized 1:12 Scale Autonomous Race Car for Benchmarking and Education
papers.authors: Koneshka Bandyopadhyay, Ansh Mehta, Bassel El Mabsout, Renato Mancuso
papers.abstract: Open-source 1:12 scale autonomous racing platform: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (67 TOPS), 270° LiDAR, 120fps global-shutter camera, 9-axis IMU. Pre-assembled for USD 2,699, 3x compute of comparable platforms at half the cost.

papers.title: Practice Makes Policies: Bootstrapping Robotic Capabilities from Zero Human Demonstrations
papers.authors: Jialiang Li, Yuhan Wang, Haojun Li, Gaojing Zhang, Yangtian Ye
papers.abstract: HERO: self-improving hierarchical embodied agent for autonomous capability evolution without human demos. Heuristic reasoning, exemplar reuse, reflexive execution in unified framework for continuous skill improvement.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Motion Planning with Learned Trajectory Primitives and Probabilistic Safety Assessment
papers.authors: Marc Kaufeld, Dian Zhuang, Johannes Betz
papers.abstract: RBFN-informed motion planning for urban autonomous driving. Combines learned jerk-minimal trajectory primitives with analytic collision probability assessment and MPC refinement. Improved risk awareness vs benchmarks.

papers.title: Physically Real-time Infrared Attack against Optical Flow Estimation Networks
papers.authors: Shen You, Wei Jiang, Jiarui Liu, Yijian Ye, Qiuzhen Lin
papers.abstract: Real-time adversarial attack on optical flow networks using infrared lights in physical world. Generates AEs dynamically, attacks victim models directly. Compromises OFENs across varying lighting and motion conditions.

papers.title: Mental World Modeling
papers.authors: Hao Fei, Yiran Zhao
papers.abstract: Theoretical framework extending world models to include hidden mental states (beliefs, intents, feelings). MENTIS baseline: training-free, inspectable system for modeling mental-physical coupled states in decision scenarios.

papers.title: VidMap: Exploiting Temporal Structure for Video-Based Structure-from-Motion
papers.authors: Zador Pataki, Paul-Edouard Sarlin, Marc Pollefeys
papers.abstract: Bridges SLAM and SfM for metric reconstruction of arbitrary uncalibrated videos. Uses sequential constraints + global optimization. More robust than SOTA SLAM and SfM on challenging datasets with extreme motion.

papers.title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models
papers.authors: Jiacheng Zhou, Jinfan Lv, Ruixuan Li, Longtai Zhang, Yan Wang, Wenqiang Zhang, Lizhe Qi
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future observations and actions, but iterative denoising and closed-loop execution make deployment costly. QuantWAMs is a post-training quantization (PTQ) framework that aligns quantization decisions with the deployment calibration context, addressing open-loop objectives and homogeneous model assumptions that make standard PTQ poorly suited to WAMs.

papers.title: One Future, Every Robot: Label-Efficient Collective-State Prediction with Decentralized JEPA
papers.authors: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Garvilov, Sergey Muravyov
papers.abstract: Formulates decentralized shared-state prediction for robot swarms and introduces Collective-State JEPA (CS-JEPA), a recurrent joint-embedding predictive architecture whose output at every robot represents one common future token field. Uses 16-frame local history and one 64-float recurrent message per directed edge, with no global pooling or target network, enabling label-efficient collective future prediction.

papers.title: TEA-AgriVLN: Traversability Estimation Alarm for Agricultural Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.authors: Xiaobei Zhao, Xingqi Lyu, Xin Chen, Xiang Li
papers.abstract: Extends Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) to agricultural scenes, where zone traversability is more ambiguous than indoor scenes. Introduces TEA-AgriVLN, a traversability estimation alarm to improve low-level action prediction on the A2A benchmark / AgriVLN method, addressing ambiguous terrain classification for navigation.

papers.title: STAGE: STyle-controllable Action GEneration for personalized autonomous driving
papers.authors: Zihao Liu, Xing Liu, Yizhai Zhang, Panfeng Huang
papers.abstract: 端到端自动驾驶个性化驾驶风格控制方法：基于模仿学习训练,融合风格值与隐价值动作模态编码,并用偏好学习把用户驾驶风格映射为连续的单调风格值。推理时用户输入风格值即可动态控制生成的动作模式,逼近个人驾驶习惯,无需额外人工偏好标注。在典型道路场景验证了风格可控的动作生成效果。

papers.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Senyu Fei, Xiaopeng Yu, Siyin Wang, Xianzhong Zhao, Jingjing Gong, Xipeng Qiu
papers.abstract: 指出VLA模型RL后训练的critic多基于单帧观测,与部分可观测的机器人控制不匹配(状态近似问题)。提出基于轻量LeJEPA架构的世界批评家模型WCM,联合预测未来潜在状态并估计价值,显式训练critic表征捕获时序动态而非仅回归标量回报,解决高维视觉历史复杂度与监督不足的问题。兼容on-policy与off-policy设置。

papers.title: FibVLA: An Efficient Temporal Vision-Language-Action Model with Fibonacci Sampling
papers.authors: Li Lin, Wujun Xu, Weiwei Meng, Kaiwen Xia, Kang Hao Cheong, Shuai Wang
papers.abstract: 针对VLA捕获时序信息与推理效率冲突的问题,提出高效时序VLA框架FibVLA:用对数回溯采样(对数hindsight)对本体状态与视觉帧采长程时序依赖以最小化冗余;动作专家用flow matching生成动作分布,并用斐波那契递推推理策略基于实时闭环反馈生成远规划。无需重训大规模视觉编码器即提升动作平滑度与成功率。

papers.title: Safe Vision Language Action Models via Barrier Enhanced Flow Matching
papers.authors: Kasra Sinaei, Hung-Chieh Wu, Donald Ebeigbe
papers.abstract: 提出模块化安全推理框架:将Flow Matching生成模型与形式化控制屏障函数(CBF)安全保证结合。不同于外部安全过滤器作用于最终输出,该方法在模型内部的Flow Matching去噪过程中直接生成安全轨迹,用平滑Log-Sum-Exp聚合屏障对整个动作块施加安全约束,保证2-Wasserstein距离有界。无需安全数据集或模型重训,在两个机器人操作平台与2D导航基准上不降低成功率地实现可靠安全。

papers.title: BWM: A Low-Cost High-Fidelity World Simulator for Robot Learning
papers.authors: BWM Team
papers.abstract: 开源低成本高保真机器人操作世界模拟器Boundless World Model(BWM):动作条件世界模型,结合初始环境引导、动态视觉历史与时间对齐的动作条件,做有状态自回归未来观测预测。通过轨迹回放、重叠片段采样、初始观测增强构建动作对齐训练片。可作为数据引擎为模仿学习补充动作对齐rollout,也可作为闭环策略评估器(风险评估、策略排序)。在WorldArena基准与物理机器人上验证。

papers.title: RayViT: Ray-Conditioned Visual Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Imitation Learning
papers.authors: Qian Wang, Longrui Chen, Peiran Sun, Aleksandar Taranovic, Niklas Freymuth, Ge Li, Weiran Liao, C. F. Maximilian Nagy, Yucheng Tan, Tao Chen, Gerhard Neumann
papers.abstract: 针对RGB观测缺乏显式几何线索导致策略对相机扰动脆弱的问题,提出光线条件视觉Transformer编码器RayViT:将相机几何表示为Plücker光线图,分块成光线特征,用门控交叉注意力生成光线条件class token,叠加为稠密位置嵌入。配辅助余弦相似度损失提高几何感知token的鲁棒性。在RoboCasa多任务基准上相机扰动下鲁棒性提升约13个百分点,真实多任务成功率平均提升1.78个完成阶段。

papers.title: Temporal Policy: History-Initialized Action Generation for Robotic Learning from Demonstration
papers.authors: Dylan Miller, Martin Jagersand
papers.abstract: 提出基于随机插值(stochastic interpolants)的生成式框架Temporal Policy,把动作生成建模为时间耦合输运问题:以机器人近期历史初始化生成流,显式耦合过去状态与未来动作序列,降低输运代价并产生直线向量场。相比噪声初始化基线将输运成本降低近一个数量级,单张RTX 4080上推理延迟19.1ms,同时保持与SOTA基线相当的成功率。

papers.title: Homotopy-Aware Corridor Generation without Predefined Reference Paths
papers.authors: Haoze Dong, Minghan Li, Meng Guo, Zhongkui Li
papers.abstract: 提出免参考路径的安全走廊生成框架:基于凸集图(GCS)直接构造凸集序列走廊,让走廊结构从自由空间表征中涌现而非受制于引导路径;将基于可见性的形变从路径推广到凸集序列以融合拓扑冗余走廊;开发自适应多尺度GCS,细尺度采样图支持局部更新、粗尺度可见性图支持紧凑全局探索,环境变化时无需整体重建。用于无碰撞机器人运动规划。

papers.title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity
papers.authors: Yuxue Yang, Shuyao Shang, Jiahe Wang, Zitong Zhou, Liang Tan, Junhan Zeng, Ruizhi Li, Junyan Li, Yu Liu, Xiao Yang, Yong Li, Jun Zhu, Hongsheng Li, Tieniu Tan, Lue Fan, Zhaoxiang Zhang
papers.abstract: 提出WorldExam世界模型分层诊断基准,跨越四层:视觉质量、控制遵循、空间一致性与世界反应性(World Reactivity)。包含1474个案例8个专门任务,支持camera/action/language三种驱动范式统一评估。World Reactivity层评估场景条件化反应与目标导向行为。评测20个代表模型发现明显能力分裂:camera驱动擅长相机控制但不支持动态交互,action驱动控制主体更精确但世界常无响应,language驱动交互更好但复杂控制遵循较差,没有模型兼具广泛任务覆盖与稳定强性能。

papers.title: DF³: World Modeling via Decoder-Free Feature Forecasting in Autonomous Navigation
papers.authors: Jiaming Chen, Guoan Xu, Aoshen Huang, Haozhuo Zhang, Yang Li, Wei Pan
papers.abstract: 提出Decoder-Free Feature Forecasting (DF³)框架,完全在潜空间建模世界演化并直接派生任务输出,彻底消除解码器瓶颈。将可学习空间查询注入冻结视觉基础模型的末端块,直接提取未来状态表示;经轻量统一Motion-Aware Context Fusion (MACF)机制,融合粗粒度光流warping与细粒度潜特征交叉相关,显式对齐预测下一帧特征;专用任务查询探测预测特征用于下游任务。公开基准与机器人仿真器零样本部署显示,性能与SOTA相当同时效率与灵活性更优。

papers.title: MoRAL: Sensor-Grounded BEV Reasoning for Compact VLMs toward Edge-Oriented Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Ambarish Govindarajulu Kaliamurthi, Kaikai Liu
papers.abstract: 提出MoRAL两阶段微调流水线,教Cosmos-Reason2-2B先读物理编码BEV表示再推理驾驶决策。BEV图像以颜色带编码LiDAR度量距离、簇形态编码物体类别、定向楔形叠加编码雷达多普勒速度,将空间感知外化到输入图像,推理时无需3D骨干。阶段1在6万条grounding记录微调视觉编码器;阶段2用8B教师生成5.77万条链式推理记录微调全模型(5200万参数,占总量2.4%)。在2304帧nuScenes上8类问题中7类胜过零样本8B基线,紧急制动召回从10.8%提升到47.8%,输出退化从94.1%降到20.8%,整条流水线适配8GB消费级GPU。

papers.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs
papers.authors: Shuaijun Liu, Qifu Wen, Shuyang Hao, Qi Luo, Chenglong Zhang, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Ningxin Su
papers.abstract: 提出CoWAM选择性干预层,将机器人策略(双臂)的同步、角色兼容与碰撞收敛表达为协调契约(coordination contracts)。每个契约结合类型化可接受性检查、事件条件验证与校准干预门。除非候补动作满足所有激活义务并提供清晰低风险改进,否则保留名义动作;名义动作不可接受时启用预定义弃权回退。8个模拟双臂任务上,相比仅契约变体协调有效选择提升16.7个百分点,闭环成功较最强选择基线提升9.6个百分点,有害干预低于1%。

papers.title: Faster-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Deep Action Modules?
papers.authors: Liheng Ma, Rui Heng Yang, Zhanguang Zhang, Mateo Clemente, Ziwen Hu, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang
papers.abstract: 引入Dock of Transformer (DoT)视频中心设计原则:将预训练视频Transformer视为表示枢纽,通过对接接口连接轻量输出头,允许灵活输出头设计并直接访问骨干所有层表示。Faster-WAM将单层动作头dock到30层视频骨干,对接接口融合所有视频层键值并应用RoPE重对齐。无需额外具身预训练即达LIBERO与RoboTwin 2.0竞争性能,且LIBERO-Plus上OOD泛化强;端到端延迟66.5ms,较Fast-WAM提速3.2×,证明世界动作模型不必须深动作模块。

papers.title: World Action Models in Real Time: An Empirical Study of Smooth Execution via Asynchronous Deployment
papers.authors: Motubrain Team
papers.abstract: 实证研究WAM异步部署策略,通过重叠模型推理与动作执行实现响应平滑控制。比较六种策略:同步执行、纯异步切换、事后动作混合、去噪时混合、推理时速度引导、前缀条件生成,在10Hz双臂机器人设置上评估。针对WAM迭代去噪产生固定视界动作块导致高推理延迟引起的停顿、陈旧动作与不连续问题,给出实践经验。

papers.title: Why Does Action Chunking Improve Behavioral Cloning Performance in Robotic Control?
papers.authors: Filippo Lazzati, Kyle Stachowicz, William Chen, Alberto Maria Metelli, Andrew Wagenmaker, Sergey Levine
papers.abstract: 系统性实证研究动作分块(action chunking)为何提升机器人控制策略性能。在仿真与真实世界严格实验中,证实现有假设(时间一致性、视界缩减、表征学习)均无法解释其成功。Levine团队工作,揭示动作分块成功的确切机制,对行为克隆与扩散策略设计有基础性指导意义。

papers.title: ChainVLA: Chaining Vision-Language-Action Queries through a Unified Execution State for Long-Horizon Manipulation
papers.authors: Yuzhi Huang, Weijue Bu, Ziyi Xiong, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang
papers.abstract: 提出1.2B参数VLA策略ChainVLA,通过联合可修正执行状态串联连续查询以处理长视界操作。Progress Context以循环Working State加稀疏事件记忆承载观测派生的任务进度;Motion Tail将前一预测未执行续段喂入状态构建与动作生成。RMBench平均成功率62.8%,四套LIBERO平均98.8%;移除Motion Tail或Progress Context后RMBench成功率分别降至11.2%与3.0%,不对称消融符合运动连续性帮助保留推任务进度观测流。

papers.title: Look Where It Matters: Adaptive Visual Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Jin Cui, Yanbin Hu, Xinyue Long, Linkai Li, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren
papers.abstract: 揭示VLA视觉编码器存在泛型ViT中可考的注意力伪影,且具身策略中这些伪影与后训练习得的空间感知能力密切相关。当编码器学习物体位置、深度序、局部几何等任务相关信息时,有限全局token容量导致部分信息溢出到低信息patch token。提出自适应视觉精化缓解该问题,改善VLA对空间精确操作任务的视觉表征可靠性。

papers.title: Grounded Semantic Re-Binding for Robust Instruction Generalization in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Zhaokai Yin, Zhipeng Zhang
papers.abstract: 发现VLA模型在规范指令被简单改写(paraphrase)时性能灾难性下降,根源是架构性的而非语义理解不足:当前VLA成功在内部保留正确任务身份,失败源于动态视觉观测与文本的联合编码引入系统性特征偏移。提出Grounded Semantic Re-Binding方法重新绑定视觉-文本联合编码,提升指令泛化鲁棒性,无需大规模数据扩充。

papers.title: Ego2Robot: Scalable Robot Data Synthesis from Egocentric Human Data
papers.authors: Ye Wang, Pei Lin, Xiong-Hui Chen, Haoqi Yuan, Zhixuan Liang, Yiyang Huang, Anzhe Chen, Zixing Lei, Jie Zhang, Tao Zhang, Haoyang Li, Tong Zhang
papers.abstract: 提出可扩展流水线Ego2Robot,将第一人称人类操作视频通过动作重定位与渲染转换为机器人训练数据,用于VLA大规模预训练。经任务级小规模验证后,系统研究该范式对VLA预训练的规模化收益,缓解机器人演示数据稀缺。

papers.title: TravKAN: Fast and Interpretable Nonlinear Traversability Analysis with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
papers.authors: Daniel Fusaro, Simone Mosco, Wanmeng Li, Alberto Pretto
papers.abstract: 提出基于Kolmogorov-Arnold网络的TravKAN框架,用于快速可扩展可解释的可通过性估计。以可学习单变量函数复合表示多元决策函数,支持紧凑架构与训练后符号表达式提取;引入基于LiDAR反射率通道的全新手工特征。公开城市与越野数据集上性能优于常规深度模型并接近XGBoost;TravKAN-Lite符号表示揭示有意义的非线性特征交互,提供紧凑可部署快速解析模型。

papers.title: Learning Panorama-Aware VLA for Mobile Manipulation with Whole-Body Teleoperation
papers.authors: Donglin Yang, Haoran Chen, Xingyu Chen, Lixing Liu, Manyi Li, Changhe Tu, Ke Xu, Xiaojian Ma, Si Liu
papers.abstract: 针对移动操作中VLA策略的两大挑战:数据层面需协调移动基座与机械臂的全身示范高效采集,以及全景感知。提出Pantora全景感知VLA学习框架并配合全身遥操作数据采集,支持开放世界多阶段移动操作任务。

papers.title: SUV: Future Scene Understanding as Video Generation for End-to-End Driving
papers.authors: Yibo Yuan, Jiacheng Fu, Jiangtong Zhu, Yi Li, Jianhua Han, Meng Tian, Zhuohan Liu, Zhiwei Xiong
papers.abstract: Unified E2E driving framework that casts future Scene Understanding as Video generation using a pretrained video foundation model. Models future appearance, semantics, relative depth, and instance-level dynamics as video streams with a shared video expert, removing stream-specific visual prediction heads.

papers.title: PRISM: Privileged Probabilistic Latent Supervision for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Motion Planning
papers.authors: Volodymyr Havrylov, Faris Janjoš, Andreas Look, Jürgen Mathes, Andreas Geiger
papers.abstract: End-to-end AD motion planning using privileged probabilistic latent supervision. Investigates VLM latent-feature supervision that yields empirical gains but lacks theoretical understanding; PRISM formalizes the methodology and improves hidden-layer learning in differentiable E2E driving architectures.

papers.title: WAM-Diff2: Hierarchical AR-to-Diffusion Distillation for Highly Efficient Autonomous Driving VLA
papers.authors: Zhihao Zhu, Hanlin Shang, Mingwang Xu, Feipeng Cai, Zhuolin He, Yaoyi Li, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu
papers.abstract: Transforms pre-trained autoregressive VLA generalists into parallel diffusion policies for autonomous driving, combining multi-task visual-linguistic reasoning with low-latency parallel execution. Addresses high computational latency and exposure bias of AR decoding.

papers.title: DecoupleGS: Interactive 3D Gaussian Splatting for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Testing
papers.authors: Siying Li, Ying Ni, Jie Sun, Jian Sun, Haotian Shi
papers.abstract: Decoupled 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for large-scale E2E AD closed-loop testing. Decomposes scenes into high-fidelity static background and manipulable dynamic objects for interactive, real-time simulation with high visual fidelity.

papers.title: Deferred Exposure of Future Trajectories for Verifiable Reasoning in Autonomous Driving VLMs
papers.authors: Zixuan Huang, Yang Zhou, Kaixuan Wang, Guli Zhang, Hongyan Xie, Yakun Zhu, Hao Geng, Xiaozhi Chen
papers.abstract: Identifies trajectory anchoring bias in AD VLA models where annotation pipelines expose teachers to ground-truth future trajectories, causing less causally faithful CoTs and severe hallucinations. Proposes deferring exposure of future trajectories to improve verifiable reasoning.

papers.title: STAR-VLM: Spatiotemporal Grounding Vision-Language Models for Motion and Velocity Estimation via Automotive Radar Supervision
papers.authors: Pou-Chun Kung, Aryaman Rao, Utkrisht Sahai, Hemanth Murali, Yi Liu, Rui-Yu Lin, Katherine A. Skinner
papers.abstract: Improves spatiotemporal and metric reasoning of VLMs for auto-labeling and E2E AD using automotive radar supervision. Avoids complex preprocessing, human annotations, and synthetic data, enabling scalable metric motion/velocity estimation without sim-to-real gaps.

papers.title: Driver2Map: Imitating Human Driving for Online High-Definition Map Construction
papers.authors: Pan Yin, Runtian Xia, Weisong Kuang, Kaiyu Li, Cong Zhao, Xiangyong Cao
papers.abstract: Online HD map construction model inspired by human drivers, fusing onboard multi-view cameras, standard-definition maps, and satellite images. Addresses modality and perspective differences in fusing heterogeneous map sources.

papers.title: SIPTraj: Map-Free End-to-End Trajectory Prediction via Physics-Guided Scene Interaction
papers.authors: Feifei Liu, Zejun Wei, Haozhe Wang, Yazhi Ye, Yuying Zhang, Jintao Cheng, Chi Man Vong, Xieyuanli Chen
papers.abstract: Map-free trajectory prediction of surrounding agents using sensor-derived BEV features without HD map lane topology priors. Uses physics-guided scene interaction to encode kinematic constraints and physical feasibility in data-driven predictors.

papers.title: ETA: A New Agentic Paradigm for Embodied Tasks
papers.authors: Yitong Chen, Zezheng Huai, Sixian Li, Yubang Wang, Haozhe Zhang, Yifei Zhang, Hechang Chen, Jingjing Gong
papers.abstract: Introduces Embodied Task Agent (ETA), a new paradigm for extendable embodied intelligence that moves beyond end-to-end observation-to-action, aiming for controllability, inspectability, and long-horizon task execution in unfamiliar environments.

papers.title: Outcome-Guided Distillation: A Teacher-Student Framework to Advance VLM Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Zeyu Dong, Yimin Zhu, Yu Wu, Yu Sun
papers.abstract: Teacher-student framework integrating structured reasoning and geometric precision to advance VLM reasoning in E2E AD without relying on potentially flawed pre-generated annotations or costly human labeling.

papers.title: muSync-GS: Physics-Synchronized Driving Video Synthesis for Weather and Geometric Road Hazards
papers.authors: Yang Chen, Yicheng Zhu, Tao Li, Zilin Bian
papers.abstract: High-quality driving data are essential for autonomous-driving systems and generative world models. However, rare and safety-critical scenarios involving adverse weather, braking under low tire--road friction, and uneven road geometry are costly and risky to collect at scale. Existing video-generation and 3D Gaussian editing methods can modify weather appearance or road geometry, but typically do not couple these edits with tire--road interaction and vehicle dynamics. papers.title: NCGR: Noise-Conditional Gated Rectification for Camera Extrinsic Perturbations in BEV 3D Object Detection
papers.authors: Wenbin Pan, Wanhao Liu, Liwei Luo, Panshuo Li, Yong Xu, Renquan Lu
papers.abstract: Camera-based bird's-eye-view (BEV) 3D detection typically assumes accurate and fixed camera extrinsics. In detectors using spatial cross-attention (SCA), extrinsic perturbations displace the image-plane projections of BEV reference points, causing queries to sample features from incorrect regions and degrading detection performance. To address this failure mode, Noise-Conditional Gated Rectification (NCGR) is proposed to compensate for projection errors without explicitly estimating a full six-degree-of-freedom extrinsic correction. papers.title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models
papers.authors: Shanglin Yuan, Weiheng Zhao, Xin Shi, Haoyi Jiang, Xianda Guo, Liu Liu
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) learn action-relevant representations by predicting how the observed world will evolve. Most existing WAMs define this future in RGB space, where task-relevant state transitions are entangled with nuisance variations in texture, illumination, background, and viewpoint. We argue that WAMs should explicitly predict action-relevant future state rather than relying on RGB prediction alone. papers.title: Overcoming Statistical Bias in Action-Controllable World Models
papers.authors: Yuhong Shi, Zhenhao Chu, Jie Wei, Jun Hao, Jianyi Liu, Jingwen Fu
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models aim to predict how visual environments evolve under an agent's actions. Yet future frames are often highly predictable from visual inertia and recurring motion patterns alone. This creates a shortcut: models can fit the data by exploiting statistical biases without making their visible dynamics meaningfully depend on the action. As a result, different actions may produce similar futures, while motion may persist even under zero action. The key question is how to reduce reliance on statistical shortcuts from dominating action-conditioned prediction. We argue that

papers.title: Quo Vadis, World Modeling?
papers.authors: Yu Yang, Xuemeng Yang, Licheng Wen, Lingdong Kong, Xiaobin Hu, Dongyue Lu, Wei Chow, Xiyan Huang, Yuxiang Feng, Yue Liao, Jianbiao Mei, Daocheng Fu, Rong Wu, Pinlong Cai, Ran Yi, Ying Tai, Jiangning Zhang, Botian Shi, Yong Liu, Shuicheng Yan
papers.abstract: Continually improving agents require dynamic interaction feedback beyond static supervision, yet direct real-environment interaction is costly, slow, unsafe, and hard to parallelize. World modeling offers a natural intermediate proxy that allows agents to query lower-cost, more controllable feedback before committing to real actions. Classical world models instantiate this proxy primarily through future physical-state prediction, a formulation useful yet narrow for agents that require actionable feedback beyond raw state transitions. In this work, we conceptualize Agent-Centric Interactive World Proxies, shifting the fundamental paradigm from physical state transitions to agent-usable information transitions, such as execution outcomes, retrieved experiences or skills, and verification signals, broadening the scope of world modeling to provide versatile feedback for continually improving agents. To systematically map this design space, we organize world proxies into six functional forms based on their feedback modalities: dynamics, spatial, execution, memory/experience, skill, and reward/verification proxies, which together characterize the primary ways world modeling serves agent improvement. We further analyze how these proxies empower agents across three progressive levels: L.1 Inference-Time Guidance, where proxy outputs enrich in-context information for superior decisions; L.2 Training-Time Optimization, where proxy outputs yield rewards, critiques, or synthetic rollouts for policy learning; and L.3 Agent-Proxy Co-Evolution, where real-environment evidence continuously updates both the proxy and the agent for co-evolution. Ultimately, this work recasts world modeling into an agent-centric paradigm, establishing a roadmap for building world proxies that empower agents to plan better, learn faster, and evolve continually.

papers.title: SG-WAM: Self-Guided World Modeling in Geometry-Aware Policy Space
papers.authors: Ruiteng Zhao, Zhengshen Zhang, Yue Su, Wenshuo Wang, Jiahui Li, Zhiyuan Yang, Francis E. H. Tay, Marcelo H. Ang, Haiyue Zhu
papers.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) couple action generation with prediction of future states. Their effectiveness depends on whether future dynamics are modeled in a space that is both aligned with action generation and sufficiently geometry-aware to capture where and how actions change the scene. Existing WAMs typically satisfy only part of this requirement, relying on either perceptually heavy observation-space targets or auxiliary latent spaces that are not jointly structured for action relevance and geometry. We propose SG-WAM, a self-guided framework that learns geometry-aware action-conditioned dynamics directly in the policy-derived representation space. SG-WAM introduces learnable dynamics tokens and a Self-Guided World Predictor that forecasts their future latent states conditioned on intervening robot actions. Prediction targets are generated by an exponential moving average copy of the same policy backbone, providing stable supervision within the representation family used by the action expert. Geometric supervision further structures the policy image-token representations, providing spatially grounded context for the dynamics tokens and yielding a future-alignment space that is both action-relevant and geometry-aware. Latent future prediction, geometric grounding, and flow-matching action generation are jointly optimized end-to-end in a unified framework. Built on a 0.9B model without large-scale embodied pretraining, SG-WAM achieves 98.5% average success on LIBERO and 73% on LIBERO-Plus, while outperforming strong baselines in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution real-world evaluations.

papers.title: Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction: Bridging Long Horizons via Dynamical Guidance
papers.authors: Xiucong Zhao, Jindong Tian, Hao Miao
papers.abstract: Forecasting precise future motion of surrounding agents is essential for reliable autonomous vehicles. However, as the demand for longer prediction horizons increases, existing endpoint-completion or iterative-refine methods increasingly struggle with weak guidance and compounding errors. To tackle the long-horizon prediction challenge, we propose Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction (PCTP). By introducing ``pivots'' and focusing on predicting pivot points along extended trajectories, we divide the long-term prediction task into short-term sub-tasks at various scales. Specifically, PCTP decouples the long-term trajectory predicting process into two processes: pivot prediction and pivot-based trajectory refinement. The pivot prediction process aims to utilize global map context and agent-to-agent interactions to identify these ``pivot points'', while the pivot-based trajectory refinement process focuses on local map details and refines the short-term trajectory based on predicted ``pivot points''. Compared with existing methods, PCTP provides more intermediate guidance while reducing compounding errors. Moreover, PCTP is a flexible approach that can be integrated into most state-of-the-art trajectory prediction models. Experimental results show that PCTP improves the prediction accuracy of leading models on both Argoverse I and Argoverse II datasets with minimal impact on model size. Specifically, PCTP combined with QCNet outperforms all published ensemble-free methods on the Argoverse II leaderboard at submission.

papers.title: GUARD: Grounding Uncertainty and Ablation-Based Risk Detection for Diffusion-Based VLAs
papers.authors: Suhas Hegde, Jitendra Yasaswi Bharadwaj Katta
papers.abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies can generate plausible actions even when their predictions are weakly grounded in the visual and language evidence defining the task. We introduce GUARD, a test-time failure detection method that measures this grounding without modifying the pretrained policy. GUARD estimates the influence of token-indexed entries in the final vision-language model key-value (KV) cache, constructs counterfactual caches by ablating salient KV entries, and compares their denoising responses with the original conditioning. Based on the comparison, we derive GUARD diagnostic stream including sensitivity, attention entropy, modality bias, and grounding efficiency, which are calibrated online and processed by a lightweight temporal classifier. We evaluate GUARD under task-held-out splits across five policy-benchmark settings, using Pi0, SmolVLA, and Alpamayo-1.5 on LIBERO, SimplerEnv, MetaWorld, and PhysicalAI-AV. GUARD achieves the best ROC-AUC on four of five unseen-task settings and ranks second on the remaining setting, improving the average unseen-task ROC-AUC by 5.73 percentage points over the strongest competing runtime monitor while remaining within 0.19 points of the best seen-task average. These results show that directly probing action-head dependence on multimodal evidence provides a transferable failure signal across policies, tasks, embodiments, and domains.

papers.title: How Should Vision-Language-Action Models Use Proprioceptive State?
papers.authors: Yiren Zhao, Ziyang Chen, Ziyang Rao, Pengteng Li, He Zhang, Weiyu Guo, Yandong Guo, Rushi Dai
papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models almost universally take robot proprioceptive state as input, yet wire it in incompatible ways -- serialized into text prompts, projected into the vision-language prefix, or fed directly to the action expert -- and almost always as a single current frame. Three questions remain open: (1) whether, and on which tasks, current state actually improves closed-loop control; (2) how much state history helps, and whether its benefit reflects genuine temporal variation rather than added conditioning capacity; and (3) where state should enter the model -- the vision-language backbone or the action-generation module. We answer these questions through controlled experiments on a flow-matching VLA, fixing the backbone, training data, action representation, and evaluation protocol throughout. We implement five representative interfaces -- discrete state prompt, VLM prefix, action prefix, state expert, and feature modulation -- under matched implementation details, and evaluate them on 45 atomic tasks spanning three task families plus 20 composite tasks; we then sweep the state-history length from 1 to 96 frames to examine how historical state information affects model performance. The experiments yield systematic answers to all three questions, distilled into testable design principles for state-aware VLAs.

papers.title: PhyAI: Real-Time Physical AI at the Edge, Scalable Rollouts in the Cloud
papers.authors: Chenghua Wang, Daliang Xu, Dongqi Cai, Duojin Sun, Hao Zhang, Haoze Qian, Huaiyuan Zhang, Jinshuo Cui, Junbo Cui, Kezhao Zhao, Longxi Gao, Mengwei Xu, Rongjie Yi, Tam Sikyuen, Tianyue Zhang, Weikai Xie, Xuanzhe Liu, Yingying Qin, Yiwen Lu, Yuan Yao, Yuezhi Zu, Yunhan Guo, Yuxin Zheng, Ziqi Guo
papers.abstract: Physical AI policies require inference throughout their lifecycle, including model evaluation, cloud reinforcement learning rollout, edge GPU serving, and onboard deployment. Although these settings share the same checkpoint and action semantics, they often rely on separate inference programs. To unify them, we build PhyAI, a Physical AI inference engine with a single runtime that keeps architecture-specific conditioning, solver, cache, and output logic in model adapters while sharing graph execution, kernels, memory management, and parallel services. The same codebase runs vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs) on single or multiple GPUs across onboard, edge, and cloud deployments. We used the adapter interface to add MiniCPM-Robot on the day of its release. PhyAI achieves 1.40x-4.65x speedups over the official implementations of pi0, pi0.5, GR00T N1.7, and MiniCPM-Robot. On Cosmos3-Nano-Policy-DROID it reduces latency from 2.46 to 1.18 s on eight H20 GPUs (CFG=2, TP=4), a 2.08x speedup. Specialized runtimes remain faster in several configurations, so our goal is one runtime with competitive latency rather than the fastest result in every case. Detailed profiles reveal why different models need different execution policies: on a Hopper-series GPU at batch size one, the pi0.5 action expert accounts for 8.8% of FLOPs but 57.2% of latency; at batch size 32 its share drops to 13.5% and throughput reaches about 100 samples/s. Cosmos3 remains generation-dominated and gains only 14.3% throughput as batch size increases from 1 to 16. We further introduce the control-time Roofline, which distinguishes inference-bound from environment-bound control; the measured pi0.5 points on four LIBERO suites are environment-bound while Cosmos3 stays inference-bound.
